description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the everyday-Perl battery (#1994; Text::Wrap LOADS, so the s491 module table counted it as working -- "it loads" is not "it works").  PRE-EXISTING on main 268d7e00.  Probes vs perl 5.40.3: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/textwrap1.pl, textwrap2.pl, regx1.pl
  use Text::Wrap qw(wrap); print wrap("", "  ", "The quick brown fox ... long enough to wrap");     perl: two wrapped lines     PCL: DIES "This shouldn't happen"
  "abc def" =~ /\G((?:(?=[^\n])\X){0,5})(\s|\n+|\z)/xmgc                                              perl: matches, $1 = "abc"   PCL: no match
  "e\x{301}a" =~ /^\X/ ; length($&)                                                                    perl 2                      PCL no match
docs/not-supported.md does not mention `\X`; an untranslated escape that silently never matches is rule 12's worst case (the regex translator must DIE or ANNOUNCE on an escape it does not implement -- audit the translator's escape dispatch for the OTHER escapes that fall through the same default: `\R`, `\h`, `\v`, `\H`, `\V`, `\N` (non-newline), `\K`, `\b{wb}`-style boundaries, `\p{..}` forms, `\g{-1}`, `\k<name>` ... probe each vs perl and table them in the task: translated / dies loudly / SILENT).
FIX SHAPE: translate `\X` in the regex translator (where the other class escapes are rewritten for cl-ppcre) to the legacy-grapheme approximation `(?>\r\n|\P{M}\p{M}*|\p{M}+)` IF the engine's property support can express `\p{M}` (measure: [[project_next_unicode_property_regex]]; `sb-unicode:general-category` is the primitive), else to `(?>\r\n|(?s:.))` + a not-supported.md entry naming the combining-mark residue.  perl's real definition (UAX #29 extended clusters: Hangul syllables, emoji ZWJ sequences, regional indicators) is OUT of scope -- say so.  ONE regex engine (USER standing) -- no second matcher.
ACCEPTANCE: textwrap1.pl / textwrap2.pl == perl, incl. `$columns = 20` (NB `$columns` is an EXPORTED SCALAR -- task #2008 makes the importer's assignment reach the module; until then use `$Text::Wrap::columns = 20` in the guard), `fill()`, `$Text::Wrap::huge = "overflow"`, a string with a tab (wrap expands tabs via Text::Tabs), and perl's own lib/Text/Wrap t/ files if they are in the companion population.
BAR: `cl/` regex translation => full sweep + companion re/ legs (`--quick` re/ once) + bench rows with regexes in a hot loop (the translation is compile-time; FLAG any run-time cost) + guard rows in an existing regex Pl/t file, INVERSE-verified.


=== PARTLY DONE (s492c, 2026-09-21, Opus) -- and the task's PREMISE is corrected ===
DONE: `\X` and `\N` are translated instead of being passed through untouched
(they silently never matched).  `\N` is EXACT ("any character but a newline");
`\X` is APPROXIMATED as `(?>\r\n|(?s:.))`, so a combining mark is its own
cluster.  Both ride the ONE forward scan that already knows whether it is
inside a bracket class, so `[\X]` stays the LETTER X as perl says.  Guard:
four rows in Pl/t/regex-extended-mode-01.t (8 -> 12), inverse-verified.

THE AUDIT the task asked for, probed row by row vs perl 5.40.3
(scratch/s492c/probes/resc1.pl): SEVEN escapes silently never matched --
\X \N \K \p{...} \pM \g{-1} \b{wb}.  Two are now translated; the other five
are tabulated in a new docs/not-supported.md section, still silent.  Making
them LOUD was NOT done: an announcement on stderr is observable output in both
test populations, so it needs its own measurement, and the batch's budget went
on the modules.

NOT DONE, AND THE TASK POINTED AT THE WRONG THING: Text::Wrap still dies.
perl 5.40.3's Text::Wrap does NOT use `\X` -- that was an older version.  Its
loop is `(?>(?!\n)\PM\pM*|(?<![^\n])\pM+)` and `$break` is
`'(?>\n|\r\n|'.$brkspc.'\pM*)'`, so what it needs is `\pM`/`\PM`, the Unicode
Mark property.  Filed as #2060 with the measurement: cl-ppcre HAS the hook
(`cl-ppcre:*property-resolver*`), PCL never sets it, and
`sb-unicode:general-category` is the primitive.  Re-point this task's
ACCEPTANCE (textwrap1.pl / textwrap2.pl == perl) at #2060.


=== DONE (s492c) ===
SHIPPED s492c member 10 (231590d2), as far as this engine can go.  \N is EXACT
(perl's "any character but a newline"); \X is APPROXIMATED as a CRLF pair or
one character -- what changed is that \X matches AT ALL instead of silently
never matching.  Both ride the ONE forward scan that knows whether it is
inside a bracket class, so `[\X]` stays the letter X as perl says.
THE TASK'S PREMISE WAS WRONG about Text::Wrap: core 5.40.3 does NOT use \X
(that was an older version) -- its loop is `(?>(?!\n)\PM\pM*|(?<![^\n])\pM+)`,
so Text::Wrap stays behind the Unicode-property class, filed #2060 (cl-ppcre
HAS the hook, PCL never sets it).  Re-point the acceptance there.
Normative statement: docs/ir-spec.md 10-esc2.  Guard: four rows in
Pl/t/regex-extended-mode-01.t.
subject: EVERYDAY (Text::Wrap) + SILENT: the regex escape `\X` (extended grapheme cluster) NEVER MATCHES and nothing says so -- core Text::Wrap's `wrap()` / `fill()` die "This shouldn't happen at Text/Wrap.pm line 78" on any input, because its main loop is `/\G((?:(?=[^\n])\X){0,$ll})($break|\n+|\z)/xmgc`
